labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE (de-bridged): VICE runs on the host, headless, no QEMU/QMP, no guest OS, no X, no exec channel. Frames VICE_SHM_PATH->shm (the same IFB1 wire format drawshm uses), keys vicectl + the shared us-layout keysym table, audio -sounddev wav -> FIFO. Launcher stations/vice-native/x11-runtime.sh; reset=relaunch restores the checkpoint in /data/vms/streamhost/stations/cbm2/sta/golden.vsf.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # cbm2 — host-native VICE 3.10.0 xcbm2 -model 610 (Commodore CBM 610, PAL, 1982) -> commodore basic 128 v4.0. De-bridged 2026-08-16: no QEMU, no guest, no X, no ssh. Keyboard-only.

eraSoftware: Commodore BASIC 128 v4.0 in ROM, with the PET disk commands built in
CP/M via the optional 8088/Z80 coprocessor board — the machine's other, stranger half
the IEEE-488 business peripherals: 8050/8250 drives, 8023 printer
a handful of ports of the PET business software it was meant to succeed
museum.blurb: Not a Commodore 128, despite what the screen says. This is the CBM-II — Commodore's 1982 attempt to sell a serious business computer, built on a 6509 that reaches a full megabyte by bank-switching, and cancelled almost immediately.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 13 (trixie) kiosk runs VICE (xcbm2 -model 610) emulating a PAL CBM 610; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio exactly like every other tile. VICE bundles the CBM-II ROMs, so this tile needs no external media — the 610 boots to BASIC with nothing attached. NOT A NEAR-DUPLICATE OF cbm8032, and the placard says why: same green 80-column CBM banner, but a 6509 bank-switching a megabyte instead of a 6502 with 32 KB, a low-profile box with a detached monitor instead of an all-in-one, and a business market Commodore reached for and missed. The golden is the machine's own untouched power-on screen; the visitor types at the BASIC prompt through the SPA on-screen keyboard. Keyboard-only exhibit; native 704x528 window on an 800x600 X root (the doubled window is silently clipped by every root this fleet uses). See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/cbm2.md. The screen reads "commodore basic 128": that name predates the Commodore 128 of 1985 and shares nothing with it.

reset.fixture: Commodore CBM 610 (PAL) power-on screen — “*** commodore basic 128, v4.0 ***” and “ready.” in green on black at 80 columns — HOST-NATIVE: VICE 3.10.0's xcbm2 -model 610 runs on the host, headless, and publishes the emulated screen straight into the shm mapping at 704x532, native size. The bridged tile dropped -CRTCdsize because the doubled 1408x1056 window did not fit its 800x600 X root; host-native there is no root at all, so the emulated screen simply IS the stream — same glyph size, black margin gone. resetMode=relaunch, and this station COLD-BOOTS: the launcher restarts xcbm2 with VICE_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT=0 and no checkpoint is restored, because restoring a CRTC machine's snapshot CHANGES THE PUBLISHED SURFACE — 704x532 becomes 704x658, the restored CRTC register state resolving to a different screen size than the one the ROM programs. A live station whose geometry moves on reset is not shippable. Measured 2026-08-16; a cold boot is stable to 120 M cycles. The exhibit loses nothing, because the scene IS an untouched cold boot. Keyboard-only exhibit (no mouse); SID sound -> FIFO.
